title: Columbia TV threatens to 'burn your negative' over the Men in Black suits in the Dark Skies pilot

tellings.quote: an it's seared in my head. He says, "Get your guys, get no, get your actors out of the black suits today or we will shut down your production and burn your negative." [gasps]

plain: In 1995 a boss at Columbia TV, the Sony-owned television studio in Los Angeles, threatened to shut down the TV series Dark Skies and destroy its film unless the actors stopped wearing black suits, says Bryce Zabel, the writer and producer who made the show. Zabel says he was there and the words are "seared in my head": "Get your actors out of the black suits today or we will shut down your production and burn your negative." He links it to the film Men in Black, made around the same time, and names its director Barry Sonnenfeld, the director Steven Spielberg and Spielberg's company Amblin, and if true it shows how hard studios guarded the look of the men in black on screen.
